prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1124; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a vehicle that backed out of a space. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reported neck pain and was advised on the next steps for medical evaluation.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone to confirm the sequence of events, and the account given matched the first report in every detail. The claimant described the impact as a rear-end contact at low speed with a sudden jolt forward and back.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision and records the location and the parties involved. Two independent witnesses also confirmed the claimant was seated in the car when it was struck.

Entry 4: Received photographs of the vehicle damage from both drivers. The damage to the rear bumper and tail light is consistent with the impact described and with the speed reported.

Entry 5: Contacted the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as the claimant described. The other driver's statement was taken and filed with the claim.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle and noted a few old scratches on the lower panel. These may predate this collision, so they have been marked separately from the new damage for the repair estimate.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical records, which show whiplash-type symptoms that fit the kind and force of this impact. The treating provider followed a usual course of care for this type of injury.

Entry 8: Claimant reported that a small strain in the same area of the neck occurred several years ago and healed completely with no lasting limits. The prior history has been noted in the file, and the treating provider was aware of it.

Entry 9: Checked the policy records and confirmed the policy was active at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage start date.

Entry 10: Confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle lives in the policyholder's household and is covered as a resident family member under the policy terms.

Entry 11: Treatment has tapered as the claimant improved, and the most recent update from the provider describes steady recovery with fewer visits scheduled. No further treatment requests have been received at this time.

Entry 12: Prepared the file for the settlement review. The claimant's account has remained consistent across all contacts, and the documents support the reported injury and vehicle damage.
